title: Worth noting obviously that half the shows I end up seeing in 2026 pr...
transcript: Here are my top 10 most anticipated theatre productions of 2026 in 10th place, Dreamgirls which might climb higher on the list as it gets closer to coming to fruition Dreamgirls is a musical that I quite like but it's not like a big favorite of mine and this will actually be my 3rd time seeing a major production of it having said that it's still a great musical and still way overdue for a Broadway revival and Camille A Brown directing it feels extremely promising in 9th place My Joy is Heavy, by the Bengsons, who I consider to be some of the strongest musical storytellers in the business. they do these achingly emotional intimate concert performance type experiences and this one is directed by Rachel Chavkin which is it's exciting but I'm always down for the next Bengsons show and if you don't know their work you gotta check them out. next, you might think this Dog Day Afternoon adaptation starring John Bernthal and Ebon Moss-Bachrach from The Bear, is just like “another movie adaptation” “another celebrity show” but I think it could really stand out from the pack the story would work really well on stage and it's written by Stephen Adly Guirgis who's like one of the great prestige playwrights of our time we got this new retelling of Antigone by Anna Ziegler sounds really interesting this cast is pretty extraordinary and the director Tyne Rafaeli has been on kind of a hot streak recently. In 6th place this revival of the Pulitzer winning play Proof which I've actually never seen but it sounds like something I would really like more importantly though I literally posted a video about a year ago with Ayo Edebiri as one of my top 10 screen actors that I would like to see make their theatre debut. I literally manifested this so it's gotta be on the list in fifth place this revival of August Wilson's Joe Turner's Come and gone which is widely regarded to be one of his best plays I've read it twice most recently when I did a full read through of the century cycle last year and both times I appreciated it but I had a strong suspicion that I would need to see it live for it to really click for me. so it's another one that I manifested and this cast looks great. I'm cheating on this 4th place one I'm saying both of the upcoming shows at Bushwick Starr if you're not paying attention to the Bushwick Starr you're really missing out like they've always been good but these past couple seasons they've really established themselves as one of the strongest companies in the city these shows are called Gooey's Toxic Aquatic Adventure and Have You Ever Thought About they both sound fascinating and kooky and could very well be the surprise gems of the season. in 3rd place Every Brilliant Thing partly because I'm a bit of a Daniel Radcliffe Stan I've seen all but one of his stage performances live I've seen a pro shot of the other, but also I've heard nothing but astoundingly good things about this play in second place Black Swan, based on the movie Dave Malloy is my favorite living musical theatre writer I probably would have put this in 1st place except I don't actually know if I'm gonna make it to see it in Boston this year so I'm tempering my excitement a bit I often joke that Dave Malloy, the Bengsons, and Heather Christian are the holy Trinity of alternative musical theatre so to have all three of them on this list is so delightful to me following oratorio for living things this is a revival of Heather Christian's Animal Wisdom which I have never seen. she's a literal genius I could not be more pumped so it comes in first place
